label: Quasi-realism's minimal truth and an actual moral error are jointly satisfiable
meaning: The countermodel #183 asks for, so the emotivism results do not overclaim. Quasi-realism's minimal (deflationary, not robust) truth, SEP §1.1, is consistent with actual moral error: a model has a moral sentence minimally truth-apt, not robustly, not true, and accepted. The quasi-realist adds that calling a judgment mistaken is a first-order moral judgment (§4.3, SEP-MORAL-COGNITIVISM-4-3-MISTAKE-FIRST-ORDER). So on Q-MORAL-ERROR and Q-MORAL-DISAGREEMENT quasi-realism matches realism at the level of what may be said. This is the first entry of #185's deviation map, which then asks what makes the error an error.
